description.narrative:
This project will provide the targeted communities with an alternative source of water for both agriculture and livestock, in Kenya.
Two sand dams will be constructed along the river bed to trap water during the rainy season, and a reservoir to store the water. The project will also establish 8 demonstration plots at the project site. Groups of women and youth will be trained and provided with start-up inputs to enable them establish the demonstration plots. It is anticipated that crop farming using the available water will increase, and offer the community an alternative source of food.
Lack of water for agriculture was identified during the Hazard Vulnerability and Capacity Assessment in the area conducted in 2012. The community took part in the exercise and the problems being addressed reflect the priorities of the community. Mass movement of animals during the dry season was also identified as a key issue affecting the more vulnerable members of the community. Children under five years, women and the elderly often lack enough food during the dry season, and this is directly attributed to lack of water for livestock during the dry season.
Anticipated change to be achieved by this project will be: • Availability of water for agricultural use by the Lekiji community • Availability of water for livestock use, especially during the dry season • Improved access to food through establishment of demonstration plots
